Read-only metadata and aggregate coverage of the named source with pyreadstat; required construction fields and FYEAR/FYEAR-lag key coverage are summarized in work/source_preflight.json. No observation-level data was emitted or saved.
Accepted reconstruction records listed in task.json: sample record, model record, attempt_02 outcome and feasibility record; source hashes match task.json.

Prior accepted Stata handoff data/reg.dta, metadata only: 93,508 rows; lowercase numeric fyear (%10.0g, Fiscal Year) and time (%10.0g, Time (Fiscal Year minus 1987)); no prior generated data reused for this replay.
changes: The requested sample endpoint is FY2010. Read-only coverage checks found one duplicate filtered GVKEY-FYEAR key in FY2010; the accepted construction aborts on duplicates and has no tie rule. FY2010 was excluded, leaving a source-supported unique-key endpoint at FY2009 and four available added years.

The one native working-copy execution mistakenly changed SOX from the accepted FY2002–FY2005 event window to FY2002–FY2009. The cutoff must remain 2005 under the assignment; the native tables and counts are diagnostic only.

The Stata cell measured period counts using each executed fit’s active e(sample), but because the event window changed those diagnostics are not reported as verified counts for the assigned scopes. No second scientific launch was made.
limitations: The paper reports 87,217 aggregate full-sample firm-years but no model-specific Table 2 Panel A N; that count is not an imposed target.

The paper does not identify the trend estimator, fixed effects, weighting or standard-error correction. The accepted unweighted OLS with conventional standard errors remains a best-effort reconstruction.

Positive DA and Negative DA use the accepted sign-specific DA>0 and DA<0 screens. The paper does not explicitly state these directional screens; the accepted reconstruction supports them from Table 1 quartiles.
The RM PROXY standardization population is unspecified. The accepted common-sample z-score construction and component directions are retained.

The paper’s page 14 trend prose omits 2004 from SOX, while the Table 2 definition and sample-period description include 2002–2005; the accepted Table 2/sample definition controls, extended through FY2009.

The source is a current local Compustat vintage rather than the authors’ historical vintage. The predecessor reported 93,508 common-sample firm-years versus 87,217 in the paper; exact universe and screen differences remain unresolved.

The local source has current live field mnemonics; current-version correspondence to every legacy Compustat item is not established by a version-specific crosswalk. The accepted field mapping and its cited provider guide are retained.

Currency-mismatched cross-period constructions remain unavailable under the accepted exact CURCD continuity rule. The paper does not specify currency conversion, so no conversion or substitute data are introduced.

FY2010 has one duplicate GVKEY-FYEAR key after the accepted annual filters. There is no documented tie rule; the full five-year endpoint is therefore unsupported, while preflight verifies common eligible support through FY2009.

The single controller run completed successfully but did not preserve the accepted SOX event cutoff: the working copy used 2002–2009 instead of 2002–2005. Its coefficients and e(sample) counts are diagnostic only; every assigned scope is unverified, and the one-launch instruction precludes a corrected rerun.
